title: makeme. — choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Departure Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Departure Board
options.lineage: Solari di Udine split-flap boards, Milano Centrale & JFK, 1960s–90s
options.thesis: makeme. is a board of eleven destinations. You name one, the machine commits, and it takes you there. Refuses the category default: the dark gradient hero with a glowing prompt box floating in space.
options.viewport: A warm-grey terrazzo hall, full bleed and lit. A dark graphite board hangs in it on visible mounts. Inside the board, at monumental scale: 'makeme.' fixed in warm white, and immediately after it a rotating cylinder of the eleven nouns — website, codes, software, cloud, email, team, club, expert, agency, boutique, support — curving away top and bottom under perspective, blurred at the edges, the centre row framed by a hairline selection window and lit by that destination's colour. Beneath it a mono status strip that retimes as the dial rolls, then the prompt slot and one lit MAKE IT key. Below the board, a departures list of what the machine last made.
options.risk: A dark instrument risks collapsing into the generic dark-AI hero the moment the hall loses its material. The terrazzo aggregate and the aluminium hairlines are load-bearing, not decoration.

raised.raise: One message per band, and the accent colour is reserved for the active destination — it appears nowhere else on the page.
The change is visible before it lands: the board shows the pending destination and the prompt's effect before any artifact exists.
Time is a real axis. Rows carry live elapsed and ETA, and the departures list orders by clock, not by prettiness.
Colour is confined to illuminated edges and the lit centre band. The text field stays achromatic.
Direct addressing is genuine input — type a letter or press an arrow to jump to any of the eleven, not just drag past them.
Density courage: the board is full of live information, never a sparse single-word hero.

options.label: The Automat Wall
options.thesis: Eleven little chrome windows in a marble wall, each holding a finished thing. Drop a coin, turn the knob, the door opens and it is already made.
options.viewport: A wall of eleven glass windows filling the viewport, each with its noun etched on the glass and its output visible behind it. The active window's door swings open.
options.risk: It is my own top-ranked candidate, which is exactly why the roll moved past it. Honest risk: a food-service metaphor makes 'makeme.codes' read as a snack, and the vending frame quietly says 'pre-made', which is the opposite of generated-for-you.
options.case: Strongest audience identification of anything on my list — everyone understands a window that opens with the thing already in it.

options.label: Terminal Yellow Wayfinding
options.thesis: makeme. as a concourse. Each domain is a gate, signed at monumental scale, one message per yellow band.
options.viewport: Hung yellow bands at each decision point, gate number monumental, arrows locked to the edge they point past.
options.case: Holds product clarity outright — one message per band is exactly right for eleven nouns. Ties on audience identification, and it lives in the same terminal as the assigned direction rather than opposing it.
options.risk: Signage points at things; it never makes them. The mechanism has to be smuggled in somewhere the sign system does not naturally have a slot.

options.label: Algorave Source Floor
options.lineage: live-coded music, projected source over a dance floor
options.thesis: The prompt buffer is the stage. You edit the line, and on the next cycle boundary the room changes.
options.viewport: One code buffer at stage scale, the cursor line as the downbeat, pending changes flashing amber before they land.
options.case: Wins product clarity on the live-generation mechanism — 'visible before it sounds' is precisely what a generating prompt should feel like.
options.risk: Loses audience identification across the family: it is perfect for makeme.codes and actively wrong for makeme.boutique and makeme.support.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.case: Declined on product truth, not taste: a fixed 40×24 bitmap lattice cannot render Arabic, Hebrew or CJK, and PRODUCT.md commits to 78+ languages with RTL.
options.kept: Direct addressing as the entire input model.

options.label: Gyaru Magazine Density
options.case: Loses both axes. Hand-written price call-outs are the system's core device and there is no pricing to state — the form would require inventing a claim.
options.kept: Density courage — fill the page, never a sparse hero.

options.label: Pickling Brine Calendar
options.case: Loses both axes. Nobody arriving to generate a website identifies with maturation, and 'wait days for it to be ready' inverts the product.
options.kept: Time as a real organizing axis — live elapsed and ETA on every row.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.case: Loses both axes. Atmospheric optics carries no imperative and no mechanism; the product is a machine you command.
options.kept: Colour confined to hairline illuminated edges while the text field stays achromatic.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What every AI generator ships: near-black hero, soft violet-to-blue gradient glow, a big rounded prompt box centred in space, three feature cards, a logo row.
canonCard.viewport: Centred prompt box on a dark gradient, three cards below, executed at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every competitor by design — which is sometimes exactly the right trade.
